title: release gate verdict
description: The machine-validated release verdict of SPEC-008 sections 1 and 2 (EP-010 M8, DOD-042). Written FIRST, from the specification, so the verdict is validated against a schema that was not shaped around the answer. Exactly one verdict value exists and no additional property is permitted, because a verdict document that can carry extra claims is a document that can carry a claim nobody validates.

verdict.description: The four tokens of SPEC-008 section 2. GO requires every applicable clause to pass AND every mandatory external gate to be signed; until the gates are signed the verdict cannot exceed CONDITIONAL_EXTERNAL_GATES (VG-SHIP-030); a candidate failure is NO_GO; a materially invalid harness is INCONCLUSIVE.

reason.description: Why this verdict and not another, in one sentence naming the deciding evidence.

partial.description: ids whose covering gate ran but whose prompt-defined oracle and negative case were not executed. ADDED IN EP-010 M11: this counter did not exist, and the omission was not cosmetic - the verdict emitted three times reported total 484 with counters summing to 218 and unaccounted 0, silently dropping the 266 PARTIAL ids. Every token of the SPEC-006 section 4.1 vocabulary now has a counter here, so no status can be counted nowhere.

simulated.description: EP-010 M11: added so the SPEC-006 section 4.1 token has a counter rather than being droppable.

unverified.description: EP-010 M11: added so the SPEC-006 section 4.1 token has a counter rather than being droppable.

withdrawn.description: EP-010 M11: added so the SPEC-006 section 4.1 token has a counter rather than being droppable.

external_gates.description: Every mandatory gate of SPEC-008 section 9, with the participant role that must sign it and the digest they sign. An agent can never satisfy one (DOD-039), so a gate's status here is never `signed` unless a named human produced a sign-off.

release_blockers.description: The exact conditions that prevent GO, each naming its evidence. A blocker described in prose without an evidence path is not a blocker; it is a sentence.
